messages:
Mara: FYI running an entitlement-lite quickstrike today at 15:00 PT. Goal: remove stale admin grants (>=180d) for non-ownerless resources, notify owners, revoke after 48h unless a justification ticket is opened. Quick, surgical sweep not full census. Link: https://redwood.internal/docs/entitlement-lite-checklist 
Raj: I can do a staging canary at 15:10 and monitor latency/alerts. Want me to run dry-run first?
Mara: Yes, dry-run then small revoke batch. Put results in #eng-sre and here.
Devin: Before revokes we need to ensure KMS grants won't break cross-account bindings. I ran a query earlier — please sanity-check: 
```sql
SELECT grant_id, principal, created_at, last_used
FROM kms_grants
WHERE created_at < TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 180 DAY)
AND last_used IS NULL;
```
Devin: That shows ~28 candidates in prod, most are old analytic svc accounts.
Carla: Also watch ephemeral elevations. audit-bot shows 3 recent `sudo` style elevations for analytics-svc in last 30d — skip those.
Mara: Good catch. Rule: skip any grant with elevation in last 30d or an open ownerproof jira.
Raj: Running canary dry-run: `./scripts/entitlement_revoke_canary.sh --env=staging --dry-run`
Raj: Dry-run output: 7 staging grants matched, no immediate errors, no SLO regressions, posting logs to GCS: gs://redwood-audit/quickstrike/1749456789/dryrun.log
Devin: After canary ok, I'll trigger KMS binding reconcile: `kms-audit reconcile --since=180d --output=csv` then diff against current bindings.
Mara: Audit checklist step — owners notified automatically, but if owner email bounces, escalate to team lead (see checklist doc).
Carla: If owners object, capture justification in ownerproof flow (template in doc). Also add a short note to the grant: `justified: true/false` so future runs ignore it.
Mara: Timeline: canary dry-run -> 4h observation -> small staged revokes in prod (batch size 10) -> 24h monitoring -> final sweep next Tue if no protests.
Devin: One infra question: when we revoke a grant, should we also schedule a key rotation for the affected KMS keys? Best practice suggests yes for service-account keys used in long-lived grants. I'll open INFRA-5421 to track rotations.
Raj: For revokes, I'll run with `--notify-owners --escalate-after=48h` flags so we don't accidentally nuke active work.
Mara: audit-bot, schedule owner notifications and post a summary once canary completes.
audit-bot: Automated notice: entitlement-lite quickstrike scheduled; owner notifications queued (42 emails). Canary dry-run success posted to gs://redwood-audit/quickstrike/1749456789/dryrun.log
Carla: Minor snag — one candidate grant references an external partner service (partner-id: p-477). We need a manual confirm from Partnerships before revoking. Marking it "manual-review".
Mara: OK, we'll exclude `manual-review` tags from the auto revoke list.
Devin: I'll prepare the revoke playbook snippet to run during windows: 
```bash
# example revoke step
python tools/revoke_grant.py --grant-id=GRANT12345 --dry-run=false 
# logs go to /var/log/entitlement-revokes/1749456789.log
```
Raj: I'll be on-call during the window and watch for any error spikes or pager noise.
Mara: Thanks all. Small ask: if you see an owner reply that looks like a mistaken complaint, ping me directly and include the grant id. Otherwise let the ownerproof flow handle disputes. :thumbsup:
Carla: Adding a short postmortem template to the runbook so we capture any fallout.
Mara: Great — updating the runbook now. I'll post final go/no-go here once canary finishes."
